title: Can a wave-pinning polarity that builds amphiphile at the front and sheds it at the rear make c03's gated FCH micelles crawl, and does motion strip the cargo from a slow-diffusion twin but not from the walled body?
summary: The C:contained-swimmers route says to give c03's gated FCH micelles a motility drive, but it names none. Camley et al.'s (2017) wave-pinning boundary drive is a published candidate, applied here as treadmilling: amphiphile is built at the polarized front and shed at the rear. c03's W failed beyond diffusion because a shell-free twin with 100x slower cargo held the cargo as well (24x vs 27x). Once bodies move, an unwalled slow cargo should trail into the wake while a walled body carries it, so motion turns a failed control into a discriminating one; the combination itself is unpublished.

sources.cite: Camley et al., PRE 95, 012401 (2017), arXiv:1609.01764, for the boundary drive (rho - rho*)|grad phi|; re-opened by the synthesizer.
Mori, Jilkine & Edelstein-Keshet, Biophys J 94, 3684 (2008), for wave-pinning; opened by the motility sweep.
